# config init writes a starter file once and refuses to overwrite.
exec drivebridge config init --config $WORK/configs/drivebridge.yaml
stdout 'Wrote'
! exec drivebridge config init --config $WORK/configs/drivebridge.yaml
chmod 0600 $WORK/configs/drivebridge.yaml

# config show reports each key's source; the file wins over defaults.
exec drivebridge config show --config $WORK/configs/drivebridge.yaml --json
stdout '"source.state":"file"'
stdout '"source.scaena_url":"default"'

# Environment beats the file; flags beat the environment.
env DRIVEBRIDGE_LOCAL_ROOT=/env/root
exec drivebridge config show --config $WORK/configs/drivebridge.yaml --json
stdout '"source.local_root":"env"'
exec drivebridge config show --config $WORK/configs/drivebridge.yaml --local-root /flag/root --json
stdout '"source.local_root":"flag"'

# A config file with unknown keys is rejected loudly.
exec sh -c 'printf "state: /s\nenabled: true\n" > bad.yaml'
chmod 0600 bad.yaml
! exec drivebridge capabilities --config bad.yaml
stderr 'unknown_config_key'

# The starter file drives a real command: space-add picks state from config.
mkdir local
mkdir remotes
exec sh -c 'printf "[nas]\ntype = alias\nremote = %s\n" "$1" > rclone.conf' sh $WORK/remotes
chmod 0600 rclone.conf
exec sh -c 'printf "state: %s\nrclone_config: %s\n" "$1" "$2" > drivebridge.yaml' sh $WORK/from-config $WORK/rclone.conf
chmod 0600 drivebridge.yaml
exec drivebridge space add --space nas --backend generic --remote nas --local-root $WORK/local --max-bytes 1048576
stdout 'Space configured'
exists $WORK/from-config/state.sqlite

# space list reports the space and its backend kind.
exec drivebridge space list --config drivebridge.yaml --json
stdout '"backend":"generic"'
stdout '"count":1'
